title: Bengueta Patatas potato (Bengueta potato): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Bengueta Patatas potato: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Bengueta Patatas potato is a potato variety. 120 to 150 days to harvest, 23.8 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: Bengueta Patatas is a registered potato variety, also sold or known as Bengueta potato or NSIC Po 08. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2007 as NSIC 2007 Po 08. It comes from BSU NPRCRTC. It takes 120 to 150 days from planting to harvest, with 23.8 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Bengueta potato or NSIC Po 08, this is the same potato. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [potato variety finder](/crop-varieties/potato), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines).

**Yield:** 23.8 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Key facts about Bengueta Patatas potato

blocks.caption: From the NSIC registry and its seller

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Bengueta Patatas potato takes 120 to 150 days from planting to harvest. That is 31.5 days longer than the average of the 11 potato varieties with a day count, 103.5 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 23.8 t/ha beats the average of its group, 21.79. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives 120 to 150 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [late blight](/diseases/late-blight).

The pests and diseases that hit potato fields most often: [early blight](/diseases/early-blight), [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [leafminer](/pests/leafminer). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its roots have yellow flesh and light yellow skin. Dry matter is 19 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 23.8 t/ha in registry trials, BSU clones gave about 25.9 to 26.3 t/ha against 21.6 for Igorota.
**Fruit:** Yellow flesh, light yellow skin, round oval tubers, shallow eyes, dry matter about 19 percent.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: bSU clones that outyielded Igorota, Granola and Ganza and made crisp, light chips with no browning. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Bengueta Patatas potato

Potato grows in the cool highlands of Benguet, Mountain Province and Bukidnon. Plant clean seed tubers, and pick a variety rated against late blight for the wet season. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for root crops](/land-preparation/root-crop-land-preparation).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Bengueta potato the same as Bengueta Patatas?
items.a: Yes. Bengueta potato is another name for Bengueta Patatas, registered as NSIC 2007 Po 08. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 120 to 150 days from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 23.8 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Bengueta Patatas?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
